attributes.name: annotation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: assistance
attributes.description: When enabled, bubbles appear to describe objects' inlets and outlets when you move the cursor over them. When disabled, the descriptions appear in the Clue Window.

attributes.name: autoboxedit_patching
attributes.description: When enabled, clicking once on a box selects its text for editing when in patching mode.

attributes.name: autocompletionspace
attributes.description: If enabled, a space bar will accept the currently highlighted autocompletion value. If disabled, the space bar will insert a space into an object box without choosing the autocompletion text.

attributes.name: autoconnectusesmouseposition
attributes.description: If enabled, a new auto-connected object will be created just below or above an inlet or outlet that is closest to the current mouse location. If disabled, new auto-connected objects will always connect to the first inlet or outlet, though the object will be created at the mouse location.

attributes.name: background
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: checkforupdates
attributes.description: Sets the automatic update checking.

attributes.name: color
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: colortheme
attributes.description: Selects an available color theme for the Max interface.

attributes.name: constrainduplicates
attributes.description: When enabled, using Duplicate (Edit > Duplicate), duplicated objects will be placed inside the current patcher view. When disabled, objects will be dulplicated relative to original object position without regard to patcher view.

attributes.name: crashrecovery
attributes.description: Sets how patch edits are restored after a crash. When set to "Always", previous patch edits will be restored when Max is restarted. When set to "Never", no edits will be restored. If set to "Ask", the user will be prompted whether to restore patch edits.

attributes.name: default_template
attributes.description: Sets the default patcher template used for new patches.

attributes.name: defaultcachesize
attributes.description: Sets the default cache size (in gigabytes) for jit.movie and jit.playlist objects when instantiated using viddll the engine.

attributes.name: defaultglcontext
attributes.description: Sets the name of the default GL context, e.g. "myContext". When set, any GL or animation object that doesn’t have a user provided context will be added to this context. A jit.world, jit.window, jit.pwindow or jit.matrix of the same name must also be instantiated.

attributes.name: defaultm4ldevicesfolder
attributes.digest: Default Folder for Max for Live Device Projects
attributes.description: Sets the default folder for Max for Live projects.

attributes.name: defaultprojectsfolder
attributes.description: Sets the default folder for Max projects.

attributes.name: enableglobalcontext
attributes.description: Enables a hidden global context to manage all jit.world context GPU resources. When enabled window rebuilding operations will not destroy those resources.

attributes.name: export_dpi
attributes.description: Sets the DPI resolution for all images exported from Max. Options are:72 DPI96 DPI150 DPI300 DPI

attributes.name: externaleditor
attributes.description: Sets the text editor used for editing text file content - such as saved coll files, text files and Javascript code.

attributes.name: fontface
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: fontname
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: fontsize
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: gfxengine
attributes.description: Sets the graphics engine that manages the interface between Max and the real time graphics API that interacts with your computer's GPU. Requires a restart for changes to take effect.

attributes.name: hidden
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: hint
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: ignoreclick
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: jspainterfile
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: jwebremotedebuggingport
attributes.description: Sets the remote debugging port for jweb / CEF. After a port is set, restart Max and open a patcher with a jweb object that has web content loaded. Then open a web browser, navigate to http://localhost:[port number], and a link to each jweb instance in max will apear for debugging.

attributes.name: layoutbubbles
attributes.description: When enabled, a layout bubble will appear when you select and move an object that displays its horizontal and vertical coordinates in the patcher window.

attributes.name: loadbangonpaste
attributes.description: When enabled, anyorobjects present in what is pasted or restored when performing an Undo or Redo operation will produce output.

attributes.name: maxurlproxyname
attributes.description: Sets a proxy server for maxurl and related web based features. This is useful for firewalls and networking support.

attributes.name: maxwindow_dequeuesize
attributes.description: The maximum number of lines posted in the Max console per update.

attributes.name: maxwindow_fontname
attributes.description: The font name used for Max Console display.

attributes.name: maxwindow_fontsize
attributes.description: The font size used for Max Console display.

attributes.name: maxwindow_queuesize
attributes.description: The maximum number of lines that can be queued for display by the Max Console.

attributes.name: n4m_debug_log_enabled
attributes.description: When enabled, the Node for Max process manager will write debug output to a log file.

attributes.name: n4m_debug_log_folder
attributes.description: Folder in which Node for Max will write its log file, if Node for Max logging is enabled.

attributes.name: n4m_debug_log_name
attributes.description: File name of the log file that Node for Max will write, if Node for Max logging is enabled.

attributes.name: oscdefer
attributes.description: Turn this on to output received OSC in the low-priority queue.

attributes.name: oscparamenableddefault
attributes.description: Enable / disable OSC for parameters by default.

attributes.name: oscprefix
attributes.description: Prefix to prepend to all OSC addresses generated by Max. Can be overridden by changing the value in the patcher inspector.

attributes.name: oscprefixmode
attributes.description: The type of prefix to prepend to OSC addresses generated by Max.

choices.label: Do not add any OSC prefix to addresses generated by Max.
Prepend the name of the patcher to OSC addresses generated by Max.
Prepend a custom prefix to OSC addresses generated by Max.

attributes.name: oscqueryenable
attributes.description: Enable/Disable the OSCQuery http server.

attributes.name: oscqueryport
attributes.description: Set the OSCQuery port.

attributes.name: oscreceivemode
attributes.description: Select whether and how Max should respond to incoming OSC packets.

choices.label: Disable the ability to control Max remotely by OSC.
Enable the ability to control Max by sending OSC over UDP.

attributes.name: oscreceivequantize
attributes.description: Output OSC only on the specified time-boundary. The quantization can be specified in bars.beats.units, ticks, or note values.

attributes.name: oscreceivethreshold
attributes.digest: Default Time Threshold For Receiving OSC
attributes.description: Time threshold under which only one message may be received. Time can be specified in any of the time formats used in Max.

attributes.name: oscreceiveudpport
attributes.description: The default UDP port Max will listen to for incoming OSC packets. May be overridden by individual patchers by changing this value in the patcher inspector.

attributes.name: oscsendmode
attributes.description: Select whether and how Max should send OSC data.

choices.label: Disable sending OSC data from Max.
Enable Max to send OSC data over UDP.

attributes.name: oscsendthreshold
attributes.digest: Default Time Threshold For Sending OSC
attributes.description: Time threshold under which only one message may be sent. Time can be specified in any of the time formats used in Max.

attributes.name: oscsendudpaddr
attributes.description: The default UDP address that Max will send outgoing OSC packets to. May be overridden by individual patchers by changing this value in the patcher inspector.

attributes.name: oscsendudpport
attributes.description: The default UDP port that Max will send outgoing OSC packets to. May be overridden by individual patchers by changing this value in the patcher inspector.

attributes.name: oscuseparamprefix
attributes.description: Prepend /param to OSC addresses that describe parameters.

attributes.name: oscvaluemode
attributes.description: Select the type of value(s) Max should send.

choices.label: Send only the raw (scaled) value and append a /raw suffix to the OSC address.
Send only the normalized [0,1] value if available.
Send only the normalized [0,1] value if available and append a /normalized suffix to the OSC address.
Send both the raw (scaled) and normalized [0,1] values. /raw and /normalized suffixes will be automatically appended to distinguish them.

attributes.name: overdrive
attributes.description: When enabled, time-critical tasks in the Max scheduler run at a higher priority, increasing timing accuracy.

attributes.name: patcher_boxsnapmargin
attributes.description: Sets the horizontal snap margin in pixels. This causes horizontally adjacent objects to snap slightly apart to provide clearer object visibility.

attributes.name: patching_rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: patchingmechanics
attributes.description: If enabled, advanced patching mechanics are provided. This includes keyboard shortcuts as defined in theguide.

attributes.name: patchline_curved
attributes.description: Sets the use of curved patchcords.

attributes.name: position
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: presentation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: presentation_rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: prioritizeexterns
attributes.description: When Max attempts to resolve a name typed into a box into an object, search first for external objects before looking for patchers.

attributes.name: prioritizepatchlines
attributes.description: When set, patchcords are prioritized for selected over object boxes.

attributes.name: rect
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: refreshrate
attributes.description: The rate limit (in fps) at which Max will update the UI for user interface objects.

attributes.name: restorewindows
attributes.description: If enabled, Max will attempt to restore all patcher windows when restarted.

attributes.name: savedependencies
attributes.description: If enabled, dependency paths will be saved with patches that contain dependencies.

attributes.name: savesingletons
attributes.digest: Add Patchers to Search Path on Save
attributes.description: If enabled, the path of a saved patch will be added to the Max search path.

attributes.name: segpatchcords
attributes.description: When enabled, clicking on outlet starts a segmented patch cord. When disabled, you need to shift-click in order to make a segmented cord.

attributes.name: selecttextonclick_patching
attributes.description: When enabled, you can begin editing the text in an object box as soon as you click on an object when in patching mode.

attributes.name: setarrowkeysscrollpatcher
attributes.description: When enabled, if content in patcher window can be scrolled, you can scroll using the keyboard arrow keys.

attributes.name: seteventinterval
attributes.description: The approximate interval (in milliseconds) between handling of low-priority events. For advanced use.

attributes.name: setmixergbitmode
attributes.description: When enabled, edits to a patcher crossfade between the old and new version.

choices.digest: No crossfading occurs and no audio latency is added
Crossfading adds a constant audio latency
Crossfading has a minimal but variable effect on latency

attributes.name: setmixerlatency
attributes.description: Sets the latency of the mixer (to enable crossfades) in milliseconds.

attributes.name: setmixerparallel
attributes.description: Sets whether audio in top-level patchers is processed in parallel.

attributes.name: setmixerramptime
attributes.description: Sets the cross-fade time (in milliseconds) used during editing operations.

attributes.name: setnativefontpanel
attributes.description: When enabled, uses the OS font panel instead of the one provided by Max.

attributes.name: setpollthrottle
attributes.description: The number of events that are handled together in one tick of the scheduler. For advanced use.

attributes.name: setqueuethrottle
attributes.description: The number of events that are handled together at low priority. For advanced use.

attributes.name: setscrollbarmode
attributes.description: Sets the window scroll bar style.

choices.digest: Scroll bars appear when using a mouse wheel or mousing over the edge of a window
Scroll bars appear if content in a window can be scrolled
The system-wide user preference determines the scroll bar style

attributes.name: setslop
attributes.description: Scheduler performance parameter that, roughly, balances accuracy with CPU efficiency. For advanced use.

attributes.name: setsysqelemthrottle
attributes.description: Scheduler performance parameter that sets the maximum number of patcher UI update events to process at a time. Lower values can lead to more processing power available to other low-priority Max processes, and higher values make the user interface more responsive (especially when using many bpatchers). For advanced use.

attributes.name: size
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: systimerearlywake
attributes.digest: Prioritize Scheduler Accuracy Over CPU Usage
attributes.description: When enabled, improves the accuracy of the scheduler potentially at the cost of increased CPU usage. Only relevant when Overdrive is on and Scheduler in Audio Interrupt is off.

attributes.name: textcolor
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: textjustification
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: translation
attributes.description: Select the language used in the interface. English is the only option currently available.

attributes.name: useexternaleditor
attributes.description: If enabled, any situation where an external editor can be used will launch the editor. If disabled, an external editor will only be used when selected from the menu.

attributes.name: usespacesforjed
attributes.digest: Use Spaces for Internal Text Editor

attributes.name: varname
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: videoengine
attributes.description: Sets the default video engine used by jit.movie, jit.record and jit.playlist objects.

attributes.name: vstscan
attributes.description: Click on the "scan" button to active a full scan of your computer for audio plug-ins.

attributes.name: vstscanmode
attributes.description: If set to "Minimal/Fast", audio plug-in scanning will looks for audio plug-ins files, but will not test or verify them. If set to "Complete/Slow", audio plug-in scanning will load and verify each plug-in before making it available to the application.

attributes.name: wheelzoomfactor
attributes.description: Sets the mouse scrollwheel sensitivity when used for patcher zooming.

attributes.name: wiggletime
attributes.description: Sets the time, in milliseconds, of the patch cord "wiggle" animation during patching.

messages.name: buildcollective
messages.digest: Build a collective
messages.description: The word, followed by a reference name symbol and an output filename, builds a collective using the patcher associated with the symbol. The collective is named with the output filename.

messages.name: checkpreempt
messages.digest: Report overdrive mode
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, sends the current Overdrive mode to theobject named by the symbol.

messages.name: clean
messages.digest: Causes Max not to display a Save Changes dialog when you close a window or quit, even if there are windows that have been modified.
messages.description: Causes Max not to display a Save Changes dialog when you close a window or quit, even if there are windows that have been modified. This is useful in conjunction with themessage.

messages.name: closefile
messages.digest: Close a file that was opened with themessage
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, closes the patcher file previously opened with themessage to Max associated with the symbol.

messages.name: debug
messages.digest: Toggle debug posts to the Max Console.
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, toggles the sending of Max's internal debugging output to the Max Console. Debug information may be of limited use for anyone who isn't debugging Max itself.

messages.name: defaultglcontext
messages.digest: Set the default GL context
messages.description: Sets the default OpenGL context.

messages.name: dspstatus
messages.digest: Open the Audio Status Window
messages.description: The wordwill open the Audio Status Window

messages.name: dumppathcache
messages.digest: Report the path cache

messages.name: enablepathcache
messages.digest: Turn on Max's search path cache.
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one, turns on (or off) Max's search path cache. This should only be done if you noticed unusual behavior when opening files.

messages.name: externs
messages.digest: List all of the external objects currently loaded in the Max Console.
messages.description: List all of the external objects currently loaded in the Max Console.

messages.name: fileformat
messages.digest: Associate a filename extension with a particular filetype.
messages.description: The word, followed by two symbols that specify a file extension and a four-character file type, tells Max to associate a filename extension with a particular filetype. The messageassociates the extensionwith TEXT (text) files. This allows a user to send a message read george and locate a file with the name. It also ensures that files with the extensionwill appear in a standard open file dialog where text files can be chosen.

messages.name: getarch
messages.digest: Report the current computing architecture.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, causes Max to report the current computing architecture to the namedobject.

messages.name: getdefaultpatcherheight
messages.digest: Report the current default patcher height in pixels.
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, causes Max to report the current default patcher height in pixels to the namedobject (See also themessage to Max.)

messages.name: getdefaultpatcherwidth
messages.digest: Report the current default patcher width in pixels.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, causes Max to report the current default patcher width in pixels to the namedobject (See also themessage to Max.)

messages.name: getenablepathcache
messages.digest: Report whether the path cache is enabled.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, will report whether the path cache is enabled to the namedobject. (See also themessage to Max.)

messages.name: geteventinterval
messages.digest: Report the event interval.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, will report the event interval to the namedobject. (See also themessage to Max.)

messages.name: getpollthrottle
messages.digest: Report the current poll throttle value.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, causes Max to report the current poll throttle value to the namedobject. (See also themessage to Max.)

messages.name: getqueuethrottle
messages.digest: Report the current queue throttle value.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, causes Max to report the current queue throttle value to the namedobject. (See also themessage to Max.)

messages.name: getrefreshrate
messages.digest: Report the current refresh rate in fps
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, causes Max to report the current refresh rate in frames per second (fps) to the namedobject. (See also themessage to Max.)

messages.name: getruntime
messages.digest: Report if the current version of Max is a runtime version.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject,sends a 1 to the namedobject if the current version of Max is a runtime version, and a 0 if not.

messages.name: getslop
messages.digest: Report the scheduler slop value.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, reports the scheduler slop value to the namedobject. (See also theto Max.)

messages.name: getsysqelemthrottle
messages.digest: Report the maximum number of patcher UI update events processed at a time.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, reports the maximum number of patcher UI update events processed at a time to the namedobject. (See also themessage to Max.)

messages.name: getsystem
messages.digest: Report the name of the system (macintosh or windows).
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, will report the name of the system (macintosh or windows) to the namedobject.

messages.name: getversion
messages.digest: Report the Max version number.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol used as the name of aobject, will report the Max 6 version number in HEX format (e.g. 6.0.0 is reported as 1536) to the namedobject.

messages.name: hidecursor
messages.digest: Hide the cursor
messages.description: Hides the cursor if it is visible.

messages.name: hidemenubar
messages.digest: Hide the menu bar.
messages.description: Hides the menu bar. Although the pull-down menus are not available when the menu bar is hidden, menu shortcut (accelerator) keys continue to work.

messages.name: htmlref
messages.digest: Look for an html file in the search path.
messages.description: The word, followed by an object name as a symbol, looks for a file called.html in the search path. If found, a web browser is opened to view the page.

messages.name: launchbrowser
messages.digest: Open a URL in a web browser.
messages.description: The word, followed by a URL as a symbol, opens a web browser to view the URL. For example:

messages.name: maxinwmenu
messages.digest: Enable 'Status' menu item.
messages.description: When using the runtime version of Max,, followed by the number 1, will place an item called Status in the Windows menu, allowing users to see the Max Console (labeled Status in the runtime version). Whenis followed by 0 the menu item is not present. The default is for the Status item to be present in the Windows menu.

messages.name: midi
messages.digest: Configure the system MIDI object.
messages.description: The word, followed by a variable-length message, allows messages to be sent to configure the system MIDI object. The following is a list of the available options:: Duplicates the action of clicking on the Auto Setup button in the MIDI Setup window:specifies an input port,specifies an output port,is the name of the port as a single symbol (i.e. It is necessary to use double quotes). Anvalue is 0 for no abbrev (- in menu), 1 for 'a' and 26 for 'z': Enables (1) or disables (0) the port specified by. All ports are enabled by default.: Similar to, but offset is the channel offset added to identify input or output ports when a MIDI object can send to or receive from multiple ports by channel number. Must be a multiple of 16 (e.g.sets the channel offset for PortA device to 16).: Prints the names of all current MIDI devices in the Max Console. (See also MIDI Messages to Max, above.)

messages.name: notypeinfo
messages.digest: Save files with Mac OS type information.
messages.description: (Macintosh) The word, followed by zero or one, sets whether Max saves files with traditional Mac OS four-character type information. By default, Max does save this information in files.

messages.name: objectfile
messages.digest: Create a mapping between an object and its filename.
messages.description: The word, followed by two symbols that specify an object name and a file name, creates a mapping between the external object and its filename. For example, theobject is in a file calledso at startup Max executes the command.

messages.name: openfile
messages.digest: Open a patcher.
messages.description: The word, followed by two symbols that specify an reference name and a file name or path name, attempts to open the patcher with the specified name. If successful, the patcher is associated with the reference symbol, which can be passed as argument to the,, andmessages to Max. Themessage is intended for batch collective building.

messages.name: paths
messages.digest: List the current search paths in the Max Console.
messages.description: List the current search paths in the Max Console. There is a button in the File Preferences window that does this.

messages.name: preempt
messages.digest: Toggle Overdrive mode.
messages.description: The word, followed by a one (on) or zero (off), toggles Overdrive mode.

messages.name: pupdate
messages.digest: Move the mouse cursor.
messages.description: The word, followed by two integer values that specify horizontal and vertical position, moves the mouse cursor to that global location.

messages.name: purgemididevices
messages.digest: Purge the missing MIDI device cache.
messages.description: Max maintains a cache of thesettings for known, but detached MIDI devices. Sending the messageto Max will 'forget' any missing devices.

messages.name: quit
messages.digest: Quit the Max application.
messages.description: Quits the Max application; equivalent to choosingfrom the File menu. If there are unsaved changes to open files, and you haven't sent Max themessage, Max will ask whether to save changes.

messages.name: refresh
messages.digest: Causes all Max Consoles to be updated.

messages.name: refreshrate
messages.digest: Set the rate limit at which the UI for user interface objects is updated.
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the rate limit, in frames per second, at which user interface objects are updated. Better visual performance can be achieved - at the cost of a slight performance decrease in Jitter, and little or no performance decrease for audio processing - by specifying a higher frame rate.

messages.name: runtime
messages.digest: Execute a message if the current version of Max is a runtime version.
messages.description: The word, followed by a zero or one and a message, executes the message if the current version of Max is a runtime version (1) or non-runtime (0).

messages.name: sendapppath
messages.digest: Report the path of the Max application.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, sends a symbol with the path of the Max application to theobject named by the symbol.

messages.name: sendtonamed
messages.digest: Send a message to a named receive object

messages.name: setdefaultpatcherheight
messages.digest: Set the default patcher height in pixels.
messages.description: The word, followed by an integer value greater than 100, sets the default patcher height in pixels.

messages.name: setdefaultpatcherwidth
messages.digest: Set the default patcher width in pixels.
messages.description: The word, followed by an integer value greater than 100, sets the default patcher width in pixels.

messages.name: seteventinterval
messages.digest: Set the time between calls of the event-level timer.
messages.description: The word, followed by an integer value, sets the time between invocations of the event-level timer (The default value is 2 milliseconds). The event-level timer handles low priority tasks like drawing user interface updates and playing movies.

messages.name: setpollthrottle
messages.digest: Set the maximum number of events the scheduler executes each time it is called.
messages.description: The word, followed by an integer, sets the maximum number of events the scheduler executes each time it is called (The default value is 20). Setting this value lower may decrease accuracy of timing at the expense of efficiency.

messages.name: setqueuethrottle
messages.digest: Set the maximum number of events handled at low-priority each time the low-priority queue handler is called.
messages.description: The word, followed by an integer value, sets the maximum number of events handled at low-priority each time the low-priority queue handler is called (The default value is 2). Changing this value may affect the responsiveness of the user interface.

messages.name: setslop
messages.digest: Set the scheduler slop value (ms).
messages.description: The word, followed by a floating-point value, sets the scheduler slop value - the amount of time a scheduled event can be earlier than the current time before the time of the event is adjusted to match the current time. The default value is 25 milliseconds.

messages.name: setsysqelemthrottle
messages.digest: Set the maximum number of patcher UI update events to process at a time.
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the maximum number of patcher UI update events to process at a time. Lower values can lead to more processing power available to other low-priority Max processes, and higher values make the user interface more responsive (especially when using many bpatchers).

messages.name: showcursor
messages.digest: Show the cursor if it is hidden.
messages.description: Shows the cursor if it is hidden.

messages.name: showmenubar
messages.digest: Show the menu bar
messages.description: Shows the menu bar after it has been hidden with.

messages.name: showprefsfolder
messages.digest: Reveal the location of the preferences folder
messages.description: Reveal the location of Max's preferences folder in the Finder/Explorer.

messages.name: size
messages.digest: Report the number of symbols in the symbol table.
messages.description: Prints the number of symbols in the symbol table in the Max Console.

messages.name: system
messages.digest: Execute a message if Max is running on the named OS
